item.title: New display technology combines record brightness with pixels that stretch like rubber
item.description: A research team led by Professor Jiwoong Yang of the Department of Energy Science and Engineering at DGIST has developed the world's first foundational technology for an ultrahigh-resolution stretchable quantum dot display (QLED) that can stretch freely like skin while maintaining sharp image quality. The findings were published in Nature Nanotechnology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: It's likely you've already chewed and swallowed some tasty morsel today. But when did that ability emerge? New evidence points to at least the middle Jurassic, back whe... Ver más
item.description: It's likely you've already chewed and swallowed some tasty morsel today. But when did that ability emerge? New evidence points to at least the middle Jurassic, back whe... Ver más NPR.ORG This surprising mammal fossil is giving scientists something to chew on Fuente: NPR.

item.title: Use of natural gas or propane in commercial kitchens exposes workers to air pollution and dangerous heat
item.description: Restaurant workers in commercial kitchens with gas and propane appliances can face heat and air pollution at levels above health-based guidelines, according to a new study by researchers from PSE Healthy Energy, the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability and New York University Grossman School of Medicine, in collaboration with chef Christopher Galarza. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Using AI for feedback, not ready-made answers, may help students earn higher grades
item.description: Although the use of AI may improve students' performance on average, what matters more is how students use it. If students use AI instrumentally, their grades may even be lower than those of students who do not use AI at all. By contrast, using AI to seek feedback and identify missing perspectives may lead to significantly better performance than other approaches to AI use. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Coach training leaves gaps in addressing girls' and women's needs in sport
item.description: "There is a systemic failure in the training of coaches for female athletes," says Ådne Ausland, a researcher at the University of Agder. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Flexible tails could boost ancient sea predators' ambush speeds, fossil-based models suggest
item.description: Some of the giant marine reptiles that ruled the seas during the age of dinosaurs were better built for surprise attacks, while their relatives were better suited to chasing prey through open water, according to a Rutgers-led study. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Cutting unnecessary tasks shows surprising links to greater employee exhaustion
item.description: Ahead of World Mental Health Day on Oct. 10, attention is turning to the question of what causes psychological strain at work. A study by Bielefeld University shows that inappropriate tasks are not the only factor associated with exhaustion. Changes in day-to-day work can also leave employees feeling exhausted, even when the number of burdensome tasks decreases. Perceived uncertainty plays an important role. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Polymer coating tackles MXene's water stability challenge, boosting CO₂-to-methane production
item.description: A research team has developed a photocatalytic technology that improves the stability of MXene, an emerging material vulnerable to water, to efficiently convert carbon dioxide into methane. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Radio galaxy from 12.5 billion years ago may be most powerful ever found
item.description: Astronomers have confirmed a powerful radio galaxy from nearly 12.5 billion years ago. The source, TXS 2354+015, was originally identified as a high-redshift candidate from its characteristic drop in optical light, and follow-up spectroscopy placed it at a redshift of 4.946. Their paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 23. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Enzymes could unlock biological recycling of difficult plastic waste
item.description: They are durable, cheap and everyday life is now hardly imaginable without them: plastics. More then 400 million metric tons are produced every year. As a large proportion is only insufficiently recycled, the environmental burden caused by plastic waste is increasing. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: EU drops sponsorship of disinformation conference at Trump officials’ request
item.description: Lithuania and Canada were also pressured to withdraw, and days before #Disinfo2026, logos were wiped off website The Trump administration pressured multiple countries to withdraw their sponsorship of a leading European conference on disinformation, with Canada, Lithuania and the EU’s diplomatic service subsequently agreeing to do so, the Guardian understands. The conference, #Disinfo2026, taking place Wednesday and Thursday, is the annual meetup of Europe’s counter-disinformation community and has drawn hundreds of researchers, journalists, technologists and policymakers to a hotel in… Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Aisha Down in London, Joseph Gedeon in Washington and Jennifer Rankin in Brussels

item.title: Small Michigan communities feel early voting strain
item.description: Most Michigan city and township officials report positive or neutral impacts from recent state election administration reforms, but many cite the costs and staffing demands associated with nine days of early in-person voting as a concern, according to a new University of Michigan survey. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mysterious Papua New Guinea rock reveals unexpected cooling as it descended deeper underground
item.description: The discovery of an unexpectedly hot rock beneath Earth's surface is challenging scientists' understanding of how heat is distributed deep inside the planet, with potential implications for how they understand earthquakes, volcanic activity and the movement of carbon through Earth. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Australia's wildfire crisis linked to colonial land-use change
item.description: Nature, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11097-z A 1,000-year lake-sediment record from southeastern Australia shows that colonial disruption of Indigenous cultural burning transformed open woodland into dense, flammable forest, priming the landscape for today’s climate-driven wildfires. Publicado también por: Nature. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: As voters weigh incumbents, research complicates case for congressional term limits
item.description: Most voters see Congress through floor debates, campaign promises and partisan conflict. Yet about half the work done by the average congressional office involves helping constituents, businesses, nonprofits, universities and local governments navigate federal agencies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Compact CRISPR alternative uses bacterial proteins to insert large DNA segments
item.description: A new engineered gene-editing system, proven in bacteria and showing promise for use in plants, animals and humans, addresses some limitations of current gene-editing tools, with the goal of improving their use in research, crop development and disease treatment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The internal chemistry of phytoplankton changes as oceans become more acidic
item.description: Our oceans are becoming more acidic, which could have major consequences for marine life. Of particular concern is what this could mean for phytoplankton, the microscopic photosynthetic organisms that form the basis of marine food webs and produce roughly half of the oxygen on Earth. Now, a study published in Nature Geoscience has found that the carbon dioxide we pump into the atmosphere is changing their internal chemistry. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists uncover how the world's smallest flowering plant became so tiny
item.description: A new study has revealed how some plants pack the same structures as larger species into a tiny space, making them promising candidates for future crops. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: First observation of quantum spins shifting a centimeter-scale object in the lab
item.description: Modern technological breakthroughs like lasers, MRI scanners, semiconductors and quantum computers rest on the study of quantum mechanics. However, the field has predominantly focused on (sub)atomic phenomena far removed from our human senses. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 194-year-old tortoise reveals stable gene switches that may help resist aging
item.description: Researchers studying a giant tortoise named Jonathan say it's not just good genes but a lack of genetic wear and tear that has kept him going for nearly two centuries. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient spotted bat samples help researchers understand present-day population dynamics
item.description: Understanding changes in North American bat populations is critical to measuring the risk of extinction from emerging threats such as habitat loss, climate change, white-nose syndrome and other disturbances. A study published Oct. 7, 2026, in the journal PLOS One by Faith M. Walker of Northern Arizona University in the U.S. and colleagues describes a research design involving the genetic analysis of ancient, modern and contemporary biological samples from North American spotted bats. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Public health strategies used against cigarettes could help reduce appeal of firearms, paper argues
item.description: Public health strategies that helped reduce cigarette smoking in the United States could provide a model for reducing the appeal and use of firearms, particularly handguns, according to a new paper from the Annenberg Public Policy Center (APPC) of the University of Pennsylvania. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Classic example' of sexual dimorphism in fossil record actually shows nuance between males and females
item.description: For decades, paleontologists have held up uintatheres as a prime illustration of sexual dimorphism, or the tendency for males and females of a species to be physically different. Notable for their large size, prominent horns and canine teeth, uintatheres emerged about 58 million years ago, fewer than 10 million years after a space rock killed the dinosaurs, and show up in the fossil record for the next 20 million years or so. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dogs and owners disturb each other in the night, but still get pretty good sleep
item.description: Sleeping alongside your dog probably doesn't disrupt your sleep as much as you might think, according to a study published Oct. 7, 2026, in the journal PLOS One by Ming Fei Li of the University of Toronto, Canada, Lavania Nagendran of the University of Toronto Mississauga, Canada, and colleagues. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can picking up a book really improve your brain?
item.description: Picking up a book for half an hour may feel like simple downtime, but reading for pleasure appears to do more than just entertain us. Research suggests it can support aspects of cognition and well-being, while also helping us understand and connect with other people. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Seafloor sediments reveal how East Antarctic ice temporarily halted its retreat and advanced 40 miles
item.description: Off the coast of East Antarctica, researchers led by Kiel University (CAU) and the Alfred Wegener Institute, Helmholtz Centre for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), have investigated an exceptionally large sedimentary body embedded in the seafloor of Vincennes Bay: a so-called "grounding-zone wedge"—symmetrical, wedge-shaped, approximately 260 meters (853 feet) high and 65 kilometers (40 miles) long. With a volume of more than 580 cubic kilometers (139 cubic miles), it is the largest known isolated grounding-zone wedge on a glaciated continental shelf to date and constitutes an exceptional… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Deep-sea clams adjust bacterial partnerships to cope with dwindling chemical energy
item.description: A research team led by professor Qian Peiyuan, chair professor in the Department of Ocean Science at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST), in collaboration with international partners, has made progress in uncovering how deep-sea chemosynthetic symbioses cope with environmental change. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Coolcations: Tourism boom is taking a toll on chillier destinations
item.description: Rising numbers of visitors headed for destinations in northern Europe in the summer of 2026, seeking respite from the heat. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s Curiosity Looks Back After Reaching Elevation Milestone
item.description: Description NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured this view looking back at the floor of Gale Crater, with the crater’s rim visible in the distance, on Sept. 5, 2026, the 5,006th Martian day, or sol, of the mission. Just nine days prior, on Aug. 26 (Sol 4,996), Curiosity set a mission milestone by reaching 1 kilometer […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Han simulado el amanecer cósmico con un detalle sin precedentes. El resultado parece un salvapantallas de otro Universo
item.description: Unos científicos han creado la mejor simulación hasta el momento del nacimiento de la Vía Láctea . El resultado es un vídeo hipnótico que me encantaría reproducir en el techo de mi habitación para los momentos de insomnio; pero, además, ayuda a comprender fenómenos relacionados con la formación de las galaxias que nos habían tenido desconcertados hasta ahora. James Webb al rescate . Para llevar a cabo esta simulación , bautizada como MEGATRON, los científicos liderados por Harley Katz, de la Universidad de Chicago, usaron datos de los tres primeros años de trabajo del Telescopio Espacial… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: A new hope for dogs with dementia: Researchers explore gene therapy
item.description: The moment Kate Heath saw her 12-year-old pug, Ivy, sitting silently and staring at a wall, she knew something was wrong. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: One quantum material, two superconducting states: Stretching helps explain conflicting experiments
item.description: Unconventional superconductors can host unusual electronic states, but understanding what drives their superconductivity becomes difficult when different forms of order coexist. The kagome metal CsV3Sb5 has become a particularly debated example. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s Curiosity Captures Dawn Breaking on Wind-Carved Cliffs
item.description: Description NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured this panorama of sunrise illuminating distant, wind-carved features called yardangs on Aug. 11, 2026, the 4,982nd Martian day, or sol, of the mission. Scientists are eager to learn more about how the yardang layer formed. Figure A is a crop zooming in on the distant yardangs. Since 2014, Curiosity […] Fuente: NASA.

item.description: Applications are now open for our newest class of flight directors!... Ver más Tenemos problemas para reproducir este vídeo. Más información Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Artemis II Crew Moon Photo Annotations
item.description: A visualization of a dark Moon eclipsing the Sun is marked with handwritten notes in this April 6, 2026, screenshot from an Artemis II crew member’s tablet. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (in blue) and Victor “Ike” Glover (in green) and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) Jeremy Hansen (in red) observed impact flashes and their locations, which […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Abortion pill access jumps almost 50% after Australia eases restrictions for pharmacies
item.description: The number of pharmacies stocking the MS-2 Step medication increased from 2,228 to 4,107 after rules relaxed in 2023 Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The number of Australian pharmacies stocking an abortion pill increased by almost 50% when prescribing restrictions were relaxed, with researchers saying the findings suggest deregulation of abortion promotes safer and faster healthcare. A study published in the medical journal JAMA Network Open on Thursday examined the impact of changes by the Therapeutic Goods Administration in 2023 which meant the medication, MS-2… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: China’s thorium-229 nuclear clock beats Vienna’s on stability, studies show
item.description: Initial results from the world’s first two working nuclear clocks indicate that China’s timepiece is about six times as stable as the one in Vienna, according to papers published this week by the journal Nature. The clocks were developed independently but both the Chinese team, led by Tsinghua University in Beijing, and the researchers at Vienna’s TU Wien used thorium-229 nuclei embedded in crystals to keep time by the steady rhythm of the atom’s core, rather than the electrons whirling around... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Ling Xin

item.title: Mars’s oddest cloud may be even odder than we thought
item.description: Scientists using the European Space Agency's Mars Express , in combination with a state-of-the-art meteorological model of the Red Planet, have found that there may be some very exotic physics behind Mars’s most curious cloud. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: ESA at IAC 2026 – Day 3
item.description: The future of European exploration and the decisions ahead took centre stage during ESA’s third day at IAC 2026. ESA Director General Josef Aschbacher joined representatives of ESA Member States to discuss Europe's ambitions in low Earth orbit, around the Moon and beyond. The day also saw ESA Director of Space Transportation Géraldine Naja receive the 2026 WIA-Europe Outstanding Achievement Award in recognition of her contribution to the European space sector. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: I hope that when the first crewed mission goes to visit Mars, they will be able to see the sunset just as Luke Skywalker did on his home planet.
item.description: I hope that when the first crewed mission goes to visit Mars, they will be able to see the sunset just as Luke Skywalker did on his home planet. Daniel Manterola Fuente: NASA.

item.description: Fuente: Clarín.

item.title: Nuclear traces in whales' teeth help scientists reconstruct their life stories
item.description: New analysis of traces of radioactive fallout from nuclear weapons testing trapped in the teeth of stranded whales has helped scientists reconstruct their life stories. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New framework developed for moving endangered species to safer locations
item.description: A new framework designed to guide one of the hardest decisions in conservation—whether to move a species outside its historical range to save it from extinction—has been published in Conservation Science and Practice, capping a multiyear, Pacific–wide effort in which the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa played a central supporting role. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: PFAS may raise blood pressure during pregnancy. Who is at risk?
item.description: Say no to sushi and steer clear of raw sprouts. Skip Bikram yoga. And keep your hands off that cat litter box. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Techno-optimistic scientists take fewer climate actions, study finds
item.description: Scientists who believe technology will largely solve the problems caused by climate change are 23% less likely to engage in civic climate action and 18% less likely to make high-impact lifestyle changes compared with scientists who disagree with this belief. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why some people are good at math while others struggle
item.description: Why do some students dread math class while others look forward to it? New research offers a closer look at the thinking skills that may help explain differences in math ability. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hidden 'uranium hotspot' offers new clues to Scotland's ancient past
item.description: A hidden 'uranium hotspot' has been discovered beneath Aberdeen by University of Aberdeen researchers—shedding new light on the geological history of the region. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Cricket's day-night pink ball not always so pretty
item.description: The pink ball was introduced for day-night matches over a decade ago, and in June this year the International Cricket Council (ICC) approved a trial of pink balls in Tests expected to be affected by bad light—subject to prior agreement from both teams. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s Webb finds signs of Mars-sized worlds smashing together
item.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope is giving astronomers a glimpse of the kinds of violent collisions that may have shaped our own solar system, including the giant impact thought to have created the Moon. By studying 21 rare “extreme debris disks” around young stars, researchers found that their dust can reveal the scale and intensity of planetary collisions. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Taking antibiotics? Sugar may be making the damage worse
item.description: Eating more sugar while taking antibiotics was linked to greater disruption of the gut microbiome and increased growth of potentially harmful bacteria. Researchers say temporarily cutting back on sweets during and after antibiotic treatment could be a simple way to reduce this damage, though clinical trials are still needed. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Penguin poop is melting Antarctic snow by keeping algae green
item.description: Penguin poop is fertilizing snow algae blooms along the Antarctic Peninsula, feeding dense green algae patches along the coastline, a new study shows. These expanding stretches of green snow melt faster than clean, white snow, potentially speeding up the spread of snow- and ice-free areas of Antarctica. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What makes a product 'Cool'?
item.description: A teenager in Shanghai will wait in line for hours to get a Labubu doll. Meanwhile, a shopper in Ohio might drive across town to buy a robotic vacuum. Although buyers might call these products "cool," research shows they do so for entirely different reasons. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists changed how zoo lions eat. Their wild side came out
item.description: Giving zoo lions whole carcasses on a feast-and-fast schedule appears to bring out more natural behavior. The lions spent nearly three times longer feeding, engaged in more tearing and manipulating of food, and rested more heavily after meals. Their activity then increased gradually during the fasting period, closely resembling the rhythm seen in wild lions. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: When U.S. embassies stopped reporting air quality, pollution rose
item.description: For more than a decade, U.S. embassies and consulates provided independent, publicly available air-quality readings in cities around the world. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Physicists just found the ‘ghost’ of superconductivity
item.description: Physicists have found striking evidence for an unusual form of superconducting behavior in uranium ditelluride, where electron pairs organize into rippling patterns called pair density waves. Even more surprisingly, these patterns appear to survive after ordinary superconductivity disappears, suggesting that the electron pairs responsible for superconductivity may begin forming before the material actually becomes superconducting. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Brake! Time for ESA’s Hera asteroid mission to go slow
item.description: Launched two years ago today, the European Space Agency’s Hera mission for planetary defence has been hurtling away from Earth ever since. The small-car-sized spacecraft is now preparing for its single most challenging activity since lift-off: the sustained braking manoeuvres to slow it down to approach its target asteroids. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: In 1993, California's pocket mouse was rediscovered; 33 years later, 530+ have been reintroduced
item.description: Conservationists have been working to revive the Pacific pocket mouse populations in Southern California since their rediscovery in 1993. Since 2006, more than 530 mice have been released into their native habitats through the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance's efforts. The establishment of a third population in North San Mateo marks progress in their recovery. Additionally, genetic rescue efforts are being initiated to improve genetic diversity among the reintroduced populations. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Conservationists are discovering 'bright spots' around the globe. Here's why they matter
item.description: Every few years, the elders of Muluk, a tiny coastal community in Papua New Guinea, close a stretch of their reef to fishing. They do this to give these underwater gardens room to breathe, grow and replenish. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists identify ancient Egyptian crocodile whose skull is missing its nose like the Sphinx
item.description: A skull found nearly a century ago has helped Egyptian and European researchers revise part of the crocodile family tree, shedding light on the Mediterranean's prehistoric wildlife and revealing an unexpected connection to the Great Sphinx. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: Drug target could block brain inflammation linked to Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s
item.description: Blocking a receptor called P2X7 significantly reduced inflammation in human brain tissue, revealing a potential new treatment strategy for neurological and psychiatric disorders. The discovery could help researchers repurpose existing drugs for conditions including traumatic brain injury, Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, depression, and schizophrenia. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Children in improved homes face lower hospitalization risk, analysis finds
item.description: Children living in houses improved through the Healthy Homes Initiative were found to be 30% less likely to be hospitalized in the following five years, according to research led by the University of Otago, Wellington—Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka, Pōneke. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Quantum computing shortcut makes particle collisions easier to simulate
item.description: Collisions between particles at high energies can sometimes produce new particles and shed light on interactions between the fundamental constituents of matter. Simulating these collisions and their underlying processes could yield valuable insights into how matter behaves at extremely small scales. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The Incredible Adventures of the Hera mission – The space detectives arrive
item.description: Video: 00:04:19 Meet Hera , our very own asteroid detective. Together with two CubeSats – Milani the rock decoder and Juventas the radar visionary – Hera is off on an adventure to explore Didymos, a double asteroid system that is typical of the thousands that pose an impact risk to planet Earth. After their two year cosmic roadtrip, Hera and its little CubeSat companions have finally arrived at Didymos and Dimorphos – the very first Solar System object to have had its orbit shifted by human action. Suitable for kids and adults alike, this episode of ‘The Incredible Adventures of the Hera… Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Webb finds a surprising atmosphere on a scorching lava world
item.description: The James Webb Space Telescope has found strong evidence that the rocky lava world HD 3167 b has an atmosphere, despite circling its star every 24 hours under extreme heat. The surprising discovery could help scientists understand how rocky planets retain atmospheres and what the young, molten Earth may once have looked like. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 'Real opportunity' to boost low-carbon European holidays
item.description: U.K. vacationers and the tourism industry have a "real opportunity" to shift to low-carbon European vacations, researchers say. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Earth’s center is moving, and NASA just measured it
item.description: Earth’s center of mass is constantly on the move, shifting by a few millimeters as enormous amounts of water, ice, and even air migrate around the planet with the seasons. NASA scientists have developed a more precise way to track these tiny swings using laser-ranging satellites, GPS data, and measurements of how water and ice deform Earth’s crust. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Plants, people and progress for native prairie seeds
item.description: Across much of the central United States, there are ongoing efforts to restore native prairie. Returning native plants to the landscape can improve soil health and water quality and provide habitat for important wildlife and pollinators. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA's Curiosity rover captures dawn on Mars
item.description: NASA has released a striking image of dawn on the Martian surface taken by its Curiosity rover, showing sunlight bathing jagged crags formed billions of years ago. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: If you're looking, here's a "good deal" for NASA and the European Space Agency
item.description: "We are in the era of people interested in having good deals, and LISA is a very good deal for the US." Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Clark

item.title: The mind of money: Mental accounting theory checks out
item.description: When it comes to money, humans are not always rational. First introduced decades ago, the influential concept of mental accounting posits that consumers make decisions based on subjective accounts that diverge from objective financial values. For example, consumers perceive a $100 check for overtime work differently than a $100 tax refund. One is seen as earned, and the other as a discretionary bonus. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hace 30 millones de años España estuvo poblada por "cerdos del infierno" y un estudio acaba de reescribir su historia
item.description: Si hoy en día nos topamos con un entelodóntido, el apodo de "cerdo del infierno" le viene perfecto, puesto que nos parecería de lo más acertado. Y es que tener un cráneo enorme, una mandíbula repleta de dientes formidables y un tamaño imponente lo hacía el mejor animal para dominar el paisaje del Oligoceno de hace 30 millones de años . Aquí la península ibérica no fue una excepción a su dominio, pero un nuevo y exhaustivo análisis de los fósiles hallados en nuestro territorio acaba de reescribir lo que creíamos saber sobre ellos. El estudio publicado en Geologica Acta ha puesto bajo la lupa… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: José A. Lizana

item.title: Premian con el Nobel de Química a dos investigadores que revolucionaron la fabricación de medicamentos, fragancias y nuevos materiales
item.description: El jurado señaló que sus descubrimientos contribuyeron a resolver "uno de los mayores misterios de la química". Fuente: BBC News Mundo.

item.title: Scientists reprogram immune cells inside the body to fight cancer
item.description: Scientists at UC San Francisco have developed a way to create cancer-fighting CAR-T cells directly inside the body, potentially avoiding the slow and extremely expensive process of removing, engineering, and reinfusing a patient’s immune cells. Using a two-particle delivery system, the researchers sent CRISPR gene-editing tools and new cancer-targeting DNA specifically into T cells, where the DNA was inserted at a precise location in the genome. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Nasa releases striking image of dawn on Mars
item.description: Nasa has released a striking image of dawn on the Martian surface taken by its Curiosity rover, showing sunlight bathing jagged crags formed billions of years ago as the car-sized vehicle continues to explore Earth’s planetary neighbour. Curiosity landed in 2012 in Gale Crater near the Martian equator, and since 2014 has been climbing Mount Sharp, ‌a 5km-tall (3-mile-tall) mountain rising from the crater floor. The image was taken by the six-wheeled rover’s Mastcam camera about an hour after the... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Hasta 100 horas de batería y por 50 euros: así son estos auriculares en oferta que tienen audio espacial y cancelación de ruido
item.description: A falta de unas horas para que finalice la Fiesta de Ofertas Prime, todavía seguimos encontrando muy buenos descuentos en Amazon. Uno de ellos lo tiene los CMF Headphone Pro , unos auriculares que, por 49,99 euros (antes 99 euros), ofrece muy buenas características. Como siempre, te recordamos que se trata de una oferta exclusiva para suscriptores Prime. Sin embargo, puedes aprovechar los 30 días gratuitos que ofrece Amazon. item.title: Hemos encontrado siluros en una balsa de riego de Lebrija a 12 kilómetros del Guadalquivir: nadie tiene ni la más remota idea de cómo han llegado ahí
item.description: En diciembre de 2023, un equipo de investigadores encontró un pez en descomposición junto a la balsa de Melendo, un depósito de riego al noreste de Lebrija. Era un siluro y estaba a 12 kilómetros del cauce del Guadalquivir. No fue una sorpresa, pero solo porque seis meses antes el ADN ambiental de uno de los canales de riego que salen de esa balsa los había delatado. El cadáver era la confirmación de que algo se estaba moviendo, bajo el radar, por el río. La notica es que, casi tres años después, unos pescadores de Lebrija acaban de capturar varios ejemplares en los canales de la zona… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Petal 'windows' affect the abundance of microbes within flowers
item.description: Some flowers have petals with small semitranslucent sections. Research in New Phytologist reveals that these "windows" alter the amount of light and heat entering the flower and create conditions that influence microbial abundance. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Biodegradable nanoparticle technology may improve agricultural production
item.description: Farmers use a manufactured version of a natural plant hormone called gibberellic acid to improve the health and growth of crops, but it is highly sensitive to heat and light. A study in the Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture shows that loading gibberellic acid into biodegradable nanoparticles can improve grape yield and quality, making it a promising and environmentally friendly approach for sustainable agricultural production. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: New research published in Economic Inquiry reveals that ridesharing services like Uber and Lyft may reduce crime in some areas. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: The European Union is under pressure to ban "forever chemicals," but a battle is heating up in Brussels over the toxic substances known as PFAS, with industry groups seeking as many exemptions as possible. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Climate change and farming gave rise to ‘genetically distinct’ Beijing swan goose: study
item.description: Climate change and agricultural development have brought a new goose population to China with unique migratory patterns, a study has found. In an article on the Chinese Academy of Sciences website, researchers from the CAS Institute of Zoology said they had discovered a “genetically distinct” population of swan geese that emerged in Beijing over the past century. They said the timing of their arrival coincided with environmental shifts in the region during the early 20th century – namely climate... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: The world's oyster reefs could add $12 trillion to planetary health each year—if they were better managed
item.description: A new study shows that the world's oyster reefs are a precious resource that's vastly underestimated and underutilized. The authors set out to calculate the reefs' potential gross ecosystem product (GEP), the ecological counterpart of the gross economic product, and arrived at trillions of dollars in ecosystem goods and services delivered each year to different aspects of planetary health, including human well-being. But for their full potential to be realized, oyster reefs around the world will need to be restored and protected. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Arctic Sea Ice Shrinks to Its 2026 Minimum
item.description: Satellite records show Arctic sea ice covering less of the ocean in both winter and summer. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: A new way to fight gum disease without wiping out good bacteria
item.description: Scientists discovered that disrupting the chemical messages bacteria use to communicate can push dental plaque toward a healthier microbial balance. The approach could lead to new treatments for gum disease that control harmful bacteria without destroying beneficial species. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Humans may not be as hardwired for violence as we thought
item.description: A study comparing 100 primate species, including humans, suggests that everyday aggression and lethal violence did not evolve as part of the same simple behavioral spectrum. Species that frequently fight or show mild aggression are not necessarily more likely to kill rivals, while extreme acts such as infanticide and lethal attacks appear to follow their own evolutionary patterns. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: Es oficial: Paramount logró la adquisición de Warner Bros. Discovery por 81.000 millones de dólares y dio paso a Skydance, un conglomerado que reúne algunos de los mayores estudios, canales y plataformas del mundo. David Ellison queda al frente de una operación que también enfrenta cuestionamientos por concentración y una elevada deuda. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Animals may have evolved 200 million years earlier than we thought
item.description: New research suggests animals could have evolved as early as 800 to 700 million years ago, roughly 200 million years earlier than some previous estimates. If so, the first animals may have lived before or during Snowball Earth, leaving behind little trace because their soft bodies were rarely preserved. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: The Artemis Accords, to which the U.S. and its allies vis-a-vis the moon are signatories, envisage temporary ‘safety zones’ to prevent harmful interference Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: What happens in the brain when cannabis makes you anxious?
item.description: Cannabinoids may intensify anxiety by removing a natural brake on specific neurons in the brain’s fear center, particularly during stressful situations. In mice, shutting down those neurons sharply reduced cannabinoid-related anxious behavior. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: Physicist Francis Halzen has an impressively long list of academic accolades—but every October, as the Nobel Prize rolled around, his failure to bag the biggest award of them all left him "miserable," he admits. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Allen Schnibben's interest in space started when he was a child. "I picked up some books about the solar system when I was in elementary school. In middle school, I got a telescope and I started observing the night sky as a hobby," said Schnibben, a computer scientist at Sandia National Laboratories. "My entire life, I've had an interest in space." Now, Schnibben collects data on satellites at Sandia's SOHBRIT facility, a 12-foot-wide (3.7-meter-wide) observatory. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Nature, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03072-5 Most disease-associated genetic alterations do not affect the genes themselves, but instead change how strongly they are expressed, often by modifying genome accessibility. Gene expression and accessibility have now been analysed simultaneously in 10 million immune cells from 1,108 people, linking disease-associated changes in accessibility to gene expression.
